summary: The article accurately reports India's CPI for June 2026 and correctly identifies MoSPI as the publishing authority and RBI's use of CPI for monetary policy. However, the CPI base year and some category weightages are outdated, as a new CPI series with base year 2024 has been implemented.

claims.claim: India's Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation was reported at 4.38% in June 2026, representing a national average.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm India's CPI inflation at 4.38% for June 2026.

claims.claim: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is a crucial economic indicator published by the National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
claims.note: MoSPI's NSO is responsible for compiling and releasing CPI data.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) primarily uses the CPI as its key measure for setting monetary policy, aiming to keep inflation within a target range to ensure price stability.
claims.note: RBI uses CPI-Combined as the key measure for inflation targeting.

claims.claim: The MoSPI provides detailed breakdowns of the CPI across various categories. These categories and their approximate weightages for the combined (rural + urban) CPI include: Food and Beverages: Around 45-46%; Housing: Around 10-11% (primarily urban); Fuel and Light: Around 6-7%; Clothing and Footwear: Around 6-7%; Miscellaneous: Around 28-29% (includes health, education, transport, communication, recreation, etc.)
claims.note: MoSPI has revised the CPI series with base year 2024. As per the new series, Food and Beverages is around 36.75%, Housing (including water, electricity, gas and other fuels) is around 17.665%, Clothing and Footwear is around 6.383%, and Miscellaneous (which includes health, transport, education, etc.) is significantly different. The article's weightages are based on the old 2012 series.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India is mandated to maintain headline retail inflation at 4%, while allowing it to move within a tolerance band of 2% to 6%, for the five-year period from April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2031.
claims.note: The RBI's inflation target of 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% has been retained for the period April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2031.

claims.claim: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) regularly publishes detailed CPI data, including inflation rates for various sub-groups and categories. You can find this data on the MoSPI website.
claims.note: MoSPI's Price Statistics Division compiles and releases monthly CPI data, including inflation rates for various categories, on its website.

article_title: India's CPI at 4.38%: Calculate Your Personal Inflation
